RPS exposes six HTTPS endpoints that the parking terminal calls during normal operation. Every one of them is protected by an HMAC-SHA256 scheme that we ship under the literal token hmacauth:
clientId identifies the terminal (assigned by us per device).
signature is HMAC-SHA256(secret, sigBase) where secret is the decoded Base64 of the per-client shared secret and sigBase is the canonical string defined in HMAC_TerminalAuth.md §1.
nonce is 16 random bytes hex-encoded — fresh per request.

The server rejects unknown clients, stale timestamps (±5 min by default), replayed nonces (same clientId+nonce within 10 min), and signature mismatches with a 401 whose WWW-Authenticate header explains exactly which check failed (catalogue in §7).

That's the entire scheme. Take into consideration the following:
Date.now() / 1000 in JS; System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000 in Java/Kotlin.
The server rejects anything > 5 min off either way.
Sign exactly what's in Request.Path + QueryString, not the full URL with scheme/host. (Scheme/host are deliberately not signed — see HMAC_TerminalAuth.md §1 for why.)
bodyHash is over the exact bytes you send.

If your HTTP client re-serialises the JSON (re-orders keys, re-spaces, changes number format) between sign-time and send-time, the server's recomputed hash won't match yours. Serialise once, sign that exact byte buffer, send that exact byte buffer.
before being used as the HMAC key.
The stored format is Base64; the key passed to HMAC-SHA256 is the raw 32 bytes that Base64 decodes to.
Don't HMAC with the Base64 string.
Even a 50-ms retry must mint a new one — the server caches (clientId, nonce) for 10 minutes and replies 401 replay on the second sighting.

The sample also runs a ValidateCanonicalSecret(...) check at startup to catch a subtle Base64 footgun where two different strings decode to the same bytes — read the XML doc comment on that method, it's worth five minutes.

HMAC authentication for parking terminal endpoints
This document describes the HMAC-SHA256 authentication scheme that protects the parking-terminal-facing API endpoints:
A single Authorization header carries everything the server needs:
Lower-case scheme prefix. Matches the JCC IPPI scheme we already implement on the outbound side.
Identifies the terminal/client. Must match a key in Hmac:Clients (or fall through to Hmac:DefaultSecretKey).
16+ random bytes hex-encoded. Each (clientId, nonce) pair is rejected on a second sighting within the cache window.
Unix epoch seconds. Rejected if |now - ts| > Hmac:ClockSkewSeconds.
The signature base string is exactly:
The bytes signed are the UTF-8 encoding of sigBase. The HMAC key is the
Base64 value of the configured client secret (so the secret can carry binary entropy without JSON-escaping issues).

For a POST /api/parkingInit to https://parking-api.example.com:443/api/parkingInit with body {"application":"Parking","outlet":"0000259010","terminal":"000025901025"}, clientId MarinaParking-T01 and secret Y2hhbmdlbWUtZGV2LXNoYXJlZC1obWFjLWtleS0wMDAwMDAwMDAwMDAwMDA=:
bodyHash = "yXkUO7gmJ0VqxvHnQH+...=" (SHA256 of the JSON above, Base64)

If the server's recomputed signature differs by a single byte, you get a 401 with WWW-Authenticate: hmacauth realm="rps", error="invalid_signature". Common culprits: trailing / mismatch, body re-pretty-printing, query- string variable substitution, Date.now() / 1000 vs Date.now() (epoch
Two collection variables: hmac_client_id and hmac_secret.
Builds the same sigBase string the server validates.
Computes HMAC-SHA256 via Postman's bundled CryptoJS.
Stamps Authorization: hmacauth … on the outgoing request.

The dev collection ships with hmac_client_id = MarinaParking-T01 and hmac_secret = Y2hhbmdlbWUtZGV2LXNoYXJlZC1obWFjLWtleS0wMDAwMDAwMDAwMDAwMDA=, which match appsettings.Development.json. Hitting the dev API with the default values should succeed against parkingInit, entranceCall, etc. without any other setup.

When the script's debug flag is true, it logs clientId, method, pathQuery, encoded, timestamp, nonce, bodyHash, sigBase, and signature to the Postman Console (Ctrl+Alt+C).
